title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Says AGI Has Arrived, Flags AI Cybersecurity Demand
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says AGI has arrived and predicts new AI models will drive cybersecurity demand. What it means for NVDA and US cyber stocks.
body_markdown:
OpenAI President Greg Brockman, cited in the same report, offered a similarly forward-looking line: "When we look back, people will think it's about this time." Neither statement establishes AGI as fact, and investors weighing the headline should treat it as an executive's framing of momentum, not a technical verdict.


> "Cybersecurity will likely be the next major use of AI, and it's going to run continuously, and so it will be a great new business opportunity," said Jensen Huang, per PYMNTS


## Why Huang Ties AI Models to a Cybersecurity Spend


As reported by[PYMNTS](https://www.pymnts.com/cybersecurity/2026/jensen-huang-predicts-new-ai-models-will-drive-massive-cybersecurity-demand/) , Huang said cybersecurity is set to be the next major use of AI and would "run continuously," making it a durable business opportunity rather than a one-off cycle. He linked the rising security conversation to a wave of product launches from AI labs, arguing that the same model advances driving capex also raise the stakes for defense.


Per the same report, Huang noted that engineers skilled at writing code are also skilled at breaking it, a dynamic that fuels demand for AI-powered security tooling on both sides. PYMNTS also cited a World Economic Forum finding that 94% of surveyed executives believe AI will amplify both offensive and defensive cyber capabilities, and reported that the share of organizations planning higher security spend rose from 64% to 85% as leaders absorbed frontier models' cyber capabilities.
